title: Structural Analysis of Growth-Controlled Tellurium using Scanning Electron Nanodiffraction
content: As silicon transistors approach fundamental atomic-scale limitations, wafer-scale van der Waals (vdW) semiconductors have emerged as a promising alternative for integrated circuits. Low-temperature evaporation of tellurium (Te) has shown significant potential for realizing high-performance p-type transistors in large-scale circuits while mitigating the thermal constraints associated with conventional fabrication techniques [1, 2]. Tellurium, a semiconductor element, exhibits pronounced intrinsic crystalline anisotropy. Its one-dimensional crystal structure consists of helical atomic chains, which are arranged in a hexagonal configuration via van der Waals interactions. This unique structural arrangement gives rise to p-type thermoelectric transport properties and anisotropic lattice conductivity, both of which are strongly dependent on the orientation of the helical chains. However, the in-plane alignment of Te crystals when deposited as thin film on most substrates is typically random, posing a challenge for optimizing its anisotropic transport properties. Our collaborators have proposed a synthesis technique that allows to control the growth orientation of Te deposited via thermal evaporation, thereby maximizing its functional properties.
